presented_options.A: 0 = OK, 1 = any error (SQL, CLI, or IO collapsed together), with stderr distinguishing the category
presented_options.B: 0 = OK, 1 = SQL error, 2 = storage/IO, 3 = CLI usage (CLI last because it's the rarest)
presented_options.C: 0 = OK, 1 = SQL error, 2 = CLI usage error, 3 = storage/IO error

answers.rationale: Exit codes: 0=OK, 1=SQL/runtime errors (Parse/Type/Runtime/Constraint/Transaction/NotSupported), 2=CLI usage errors (Cli variant), 3=storage/IO errors (Io/Storage/Wal variants).

presented_options.A: statements run under a long-running implicit transaction that commits only when the process exits
presented_options.B: statements run without any transaction; durability is deferred to a periodic checkpoint
presented_options.C: statements inherit the transaction of the previous BEGIN if any was ever opened in the session
presented_options.D: each statement is implicitly wrapped in its own transaction that commits on success, matching BEGIN/COMMIT semantics

answers.rationale: Default TxnState is AutoCommit; each DML/DDL statement is individually committed immediately after execution, matching BEGIN/COMMIT semantics.

presented_options.A: shadow paging: mutations go to a copy page; a pointer swap at commit promotes the copy atomically
presented_options.B: an append-only write-ahead log, replayed at startup to re-apply committed transactions and drop the uncommitted suffix
presented_options.C: synchronous double-write: every page is written to a scratch region before being written to its home location
presented_options.D: ARIES-style WAL with explicit undo and redo records plus a separate dirty-page table checkpoint

answers.rationale: Append-only WAL with fsync on commit; startup calls recover() to replay only committed records and discard the uncommitted suffix.

presented_options.A: records are padded to a fixed 512-byte sector boundary; partial sectors are discarded
presented_options.B: records are written in pairs (main + mirror); replay prefers whichever pair verifies
presented_options.C: each record carries a CRC32; replay stops at the first record whose CRC fails to verify
presented_options.D: no per-record check; a single CRC covers the whole WAL file on clean shutdown

answers.rationale: Each WAL record is framed with [payload_len u32, crc32(payload) u32, payload]; recovery stops and discards at the first record that fails CRC verification.

presented_options.A: vectorised/columnar execution where each operator produces and consumes batches of column vectors
presented_options.B: push-based execution where operators drive their children forward via a single dataflow scheduler
presented_options.C: materialising execution: each operator fully computes its output set before the next operator starts reading
presented_options.D: a Volcano-style iterator tree: each operator exposes open/next/close and returns one row (or tiny batch) at a time

answers.rationale: PhysicalOperator trait exposes open/next/close; next() yields one ExecRow at a time — classic Volcano/iterator model.

presented_options.A: an inverted list built lazily on first query and cached in memory
presented_options.B: a bitmap per distinct value; looked up with bitwise AND for compound predicates
presented_options.C: a hash map keyed by the indexed value alone; collisions chain a Vec<RowId>
presented_options.D: a B-tree keyed by the composite (index_key, row_id); duplicates are naturally ordered by row_id

answers.rationale: B-tree leaf entries are (key, row_id) pairs sorted first by key then by RowId, enabling natural duplicate ordering by row_id.

presented_options.A: IndexScan and SeqScan as two variants of a single ScanKind enum so the executor only has one Scan operator
presented_options.B: Filter and Project exist as separate types rather than being fused into one 'SelectExpr' operator
presented_options.C: Update and Delete are distinct operators rather than one 'Mutate' operator parameterised by a kind
presented_options.D: SeqScan, IndexScan, Filter, Project, NestedLoopJoin, Sort, Limit, Insert, Update, Delete each as a distinct type

answers.rationale: SeqScan and IndexScan are distinct structs, not variants of a shared ScanKind enum; option A describes a design that does not exist in this codebase.

presented_options.A: inside the executor at open() time, after consulting the catalog to see whether an index is applicable
presented_options.B: inside the storage layer, which transparently redirects SeqScan calls through the index when available
presented_options.C: inside the planner when lowering the logical plan to a physical plan; the parser only produces ASTs
presented_options.D: inside the parser, encoded as a special AST node when the WHERE clause mentions an indexed column

answers.rationale: The planner's single_table_index_scan() checks the catalog for an applicable index when lowering the logical plan to a physical plan.

presented_options.A: errors are propagated via panics with typed payloads and caught at the CLI via std::panic::catch_unwind
presented_options.B: errors are encoded as strings (Result<T, String>) so every caller formats them uniformly
presented_options.C: a single crate-wide error enum with one variant per source is the return type of top-level entry points; lower modules convert at their public boundary
presented_options.D: each subsystem defines its own error type; the CLI sees a Box<dyn Error> and pattern-matches on downcast

answers.rationale: A single MiniDbError enum has one variant per error source (Io, Parse, Lex, Type, Runtime, Catalog, Constraint, Storage, Wal, Transaction, NotSupported, Cli); type alias Result<T> used throughout.

presented_options.A: table / json / messagepack selectable only via an environment variable MINIDB_FORMAT
presented_options.B: the format is fixed at build time via a Cargo feature (--features=json)
presented_options.C: table output only; downstream callers are expected to parse and re-format it themselves
presented_options.D: table / csv / json selectable via a --format CLI flag or a .format meta-command in the REPL

answers.rationale: OutputFormat supports table/csv/json, selectable via --format CLI flag; .format meta-command also switches format at runtime in the REPL.

presented_options.A: when --format json is active, the JSON value is the only thing on stdout — no banner lines, no trailing 'ok' line
presented_options.B: per-statement summary lines (e.g. `ok 3 rows`) go to stderr, letting callers pipe stdout straight into another tool
presented_options.C: the per-statement summary is written to stdout immediately before the data so callers see it arrive first
presented_options.D: --quiet suppresses the per-statement summary entirely; stdout still carries the data stream

answers.rationale: Per-statement summaries go to stderr (not stdout before the data), so writing the summary to stdout before the data would be inconsistent with the codebase contract.

presented_options.A: the heap stores rows inside fixed-size pages rather than one file per row
presented_options.B: the page size is a single compile-time constant referenced throughout storage
presented_options.C: pages are a mixed size; the header chooses between 4 KiB and 16 KiB per table based on row width
presented_options.D: pages are identified by a newtype over u64 (PageId) rather than a bare integer

answers.rationale: PAGE_SIZE is a single compile-time constant (4096 bytes); there is no mixed-size scheme choosing between 4 KiB and 16 KiB per table.

presented_options.A: all three rows — every fsynced WAL record is replayed on startup
presented_options.B: the two earliest rows — only WAL records that survive the CRC check are replayed; the trailing one is dropped
presented_options.C: no rows — a transaction whose WAL trail has no COMMIT record is treated as an uncommitted prefix and discarded
presented_options.D: an error at startup demanding manual recovery before any SELECT can run

answers.rationale: Recovery replays only transactions that have both a Begin and a Commit WAL record; without a COMMIT record the three inserts are treated as an uncommitted prefix and discarded.

presented_options.A: zero hits — every diagnostic outside the CLI boundary goes through the `log` facade
presented_options.B: scattered hits across most modules; the codebase routinely uses `eprintln!` for diagnostics
presented_options.C: hits only in `parser` and `error`, where the modules format diagnostic messages directly
presented_options.D: a small number of hits inside `exec` operators, used to print per-row debugging during EXPLAIN

answers.rationale: No eprintln! calls found outside the CLI module; all diagnostics in library code are propagated via the Result/MiniDbError mechanism, not printed directly.

presented_options.A: exits with code 2 and prints a CLI usage error on stderr naming the bad value
presented_options.B: panics with an unwrap on the unrecognised format string
presented_options.C: executes the SELECT and silently falls back to the default `table` format
presented_options.D: exits with code 1 and prints a SQL error pointing at the SELECT

answers.rationale: OutputFormat::parse returns MiniDbError::Cli for unknown format strings; the CLI maps Cli errors to exit code 2 and prints the error on stderr.
